data.name: Bhavansh
data.gender_notes: Bhavansh is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Bhavansh is a Sanskrit name derived from the words 'Bhava' (existence) and 'Ansh' (essence). It is believed to represent the creator of the universe and is a revered name in Hindu mythology. The name Bhavansh carries the meaning “Lord of Creation” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Bhavansh usually hope their child will grow to embody lord of creation and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine essence of creation and the supreme power behind the universe.
data.etymology: Bhavansh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lord of Creation.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bhavansh total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

The name also holds immense importance in Hindu Jyotish (astrology), where it is believed to represent the Sun, which is considered the source of all energy and light.

historical_references.reference: Bhavansh was a prominent ruler of the Chalukya Dynasty in the Deccan region of India during the 11th century. He is known for his military conquests and architectural contributions, particularly the construction of the Sangameshwara Temple in Kudalasangama.
historical_references.context: Chalukya Empire in the Deccan region

historical_references.reference: Bhavansh was also the name of a Jain Tirthankara, a religious leader who lived during the 12th or 13th century BCE. The 'Bhavasutra' is a scripture attributed to him, which discusses Jain philosophy and ethics.
